content: 1. Administer 2 mg/kg of penicillin orally or intravenously every 12 hours for 60 days. Switch to amoxicillin as soon as penicillin susceptibility is confirmed. 2. Doxycycline and acitretin are contraindicated due to the risk of increased intracranial pressure. Both acitretin and tetracyclines can elevate intracranial pressure. 3. Doxycycline reduces the effects of allogeneic cultured keratinocytes/fibroblasts in bovine collagen. Avoid exposure to topical antibiotics, as they degrade Gintuit. If exposed, irrigate the wound thoroughly with saline and allow a wash-out period before applying Gintuit. 4. Doxycycline and tretinoin increase each other’s toxicity through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Both drugs can cause increased intracranial pressure. Avoid co-administration. 5. Aluminum hydroxide decreases doxycycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by at least 2 hours or use an alternative drug. 6. Aminolevulinic acid (oral) and doxycycline increase each other’s toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Avoid administering other phototoxic drugs with aminolevulinic acid during the perioperative period. 7. Doxycycline increases the toxicity of aminolevulinic acid (topical) through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Photosensitizing drugs may enhance phototoxic reactions during photodynamic therapy with aminolevulinic acid. 8. Doxycycline decreases the effects of amoxicillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Tetracyclines may interfere with the bactericidal action of penicillins. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of penicillins if used concurrently with tetracyclines. 9. Doxycycline decreases the effects of ampicillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Tetracyclines may interfere with the bactericidal action of penicillins. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of penicillins if used concurrently with tetracyclines. 10. Doxycycline increases the effects of atracurium through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug due to the risk of respiratory depression. 11. Doxycycline decreases the effects of the BCG vaccine (live) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 12.
